newsitem.title: USA: Educational Development sees record FY98.
newsitem.headline: Educational Development sees record FY98.

text.p: Educational Development Corp said Wednesday it expects record earnings for its February 28 fiscal year of $0.45 to $0.50 a share.
The Tulsa, Okla.-based company, which sells children's books to schools, libraries and directly to consumers, earned $0.31 in fiscal 1997.
It also expects record fiscal 1998 sales of $25 million to $26 million, up from a record $21.3 million reported in fiscal 1997, President Randall White said in a telephone interview.

Earlier today, the company reported its fiscal 1998 first quarter earnings rose 53 percent to $463,900 or $0.09 from $303,100 or $0.06 in the same quarter a year ago. Results benefitted from restructuring and system efficiencies implemented last year, the company said in a news release.
Fiscal first quarter sales fell 18 percent to $4.7 million due to the elimination of an unprofitable library services division and also lower sales in its home business division, the company said.

White said Educational Development has initiated new marketing incentives for its sales force to stimulate growth. The incentives were announced in June and positive results have already occurred, he said.
In another development, White said the company's directors has authorized the repurchase of up to 10 percent of the company's 5.3 million common shares as market conditions warrant.
Shares of Educational Development were trading up 13/16 to 6-3/8.
